title: War years: Procope's draft and Billy Kyle going into the army first
summary: Procope was drafted in September 1943 after Pearl Harbor; pianist Billy Kyle went first, and the band kidded him with songs about the army.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: But you didn't go in the army right away, did you? When did you --
Pearl Harbor Day was December the 7th, 1941, and I was drafted in the army in October, 19 -- September, 1943. So I had those years. And those are very good years, because --
Yes. Well, Buster went in before you, into the army.
No, no, no, no, no. Buster didn't go in the army at all. It was Billy.

He was the first one that went into the army, and it was a funny thing for a man going into the army, you know, we made sort of light of it, you know. We didn't -- we tried to keep him happy and all that, because my goodness, he was a very, very good musician, and he had it all in front of him, you know, his life. He attained some of his, you know, later years, like he worked for Louis Armstrong, and he got, you know, along the line. But Billy, you know, all these songs used to come out about, 'You're A-l in the Army, but You're A-l in My Heart,' or something like that?
We used to kid him, you know. We

asked him did he know that, you know, and like that sort of. "Don't Sit Under the Apple Tree With Anyone Else But Me," you know. So we kidded him and he finally went in the army. And it was too bad, because -- oh, yes, I forgot. And we had a contract at that time to go to Rio de Janeiro. I think the name of the club down there was the Copacabana, and we had a year's contract, I believe, which for that time was a tremendous salary.
